title: Born-again self-distillation (Furlanello et al. 2018), pretraining only: a teacher trained with the 153-claude recipe for the first 40% of the wall-clock, then a fresh same-architecture student trained on the same batches with KL(teacher || student) added to its CE + MTP loss and handed to RL, on the 153-claude width-384 Lean incumbent (9,557,760 params, handoff model unchanged)
description: Idea ID: P47-family (soft targets on the same supervised positions; nearest backlog entries P47 label smoothing and P50 auxiliary supervision, no exact ID): the 300 s budget is split at KD_SPLIT = 0.4. Phase 1 (0-120 s) trains a teacher exactly as 153-claude does (Muon + AdamW, MTP, token-budget batches, orthogonal init) with the warmup + cosine-to-0.3 schedule compressed onto its 120 s window; phase 2 (120-300 s) builds a fresh model with the same architecture and init rule and trains it with fresh optimizers and the same schedule over its 180 s window on loss = CE + 0.3 * MTP + KD_WEIGHT * KL(p_teacher || p_student) at temperature 1 over the proof-token positions (KD_WEIGHT = 1.0), the frozen teacher giving one no-grad forward per step. Only the student is returned. Why it should help expert iteration: 153's val loss bottoms at ~105 s (0.0847 at step 1,435 of 4,540) and is flat after while train CE keeps falling to 0.055, i.e. the last two thirds of the budget memorize each training record's one-hot pick at positions where several next proof lines are valid; the student instead matches the teacher's smoothed distribution there while deterministic tokens stay deterministic, unlike focal loss (173-fable, 655) and label smoothing, which flatten every position. A less memorized, calibrated next-line distribution should give the T=0.8 sampler more distinct valid continuations per 32 attempts in RL round 1 and a smoother starting point for the fixed AdamW fine-tuning.
hypothesis: Dark-knowledge distillation from an in-run teacher of the same size (born-again networks) reduces memorization of arbitrary training-record choices at multimodal proof positions: the student's one-hot CE is regularized toward the teacher's full distribution, which carries the teacher's belief over alternative valid next lines. The handed-off model then samples valid long proofs at T=0.8 with more diversity across its 32-64 attempts (more RL round-1 targets solved, more new proofs per round) without the entropy inflation on deterministic tokens that made focal loss lose. Mechanism signatures: the student's final train CE stays above 153's 0.055 (predicted 0.060-0.075) at an unchanged val CE (0.082-0.092), the KD term ends below 0.03 nats, and RL round-1 targets solved and new proofs are at or above 153's 766 / 1,177. Confounds registered in advance: the student sees ~1.7-2.0 epochs instead of 4.0 and gets ~2,100 steps instead of 4,540, so part of any effect may be 'fewer epochs' rather than KD; total steps (teacher + student) ~3,500-4,100.
expected_delta: -40 to +40 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean) vs 153-claude's 687 (676/700/685), central +5; keep needs a mean > 687. Mechanism predictions: total pretrain steps 3,500-4,100 per seed (teacher 1,550-1,850 in its ~105 s of training after ~15 s setup at ~16 steps/s; student 1,900-2,300 in 180 s at ~11-12.5 steps/s, the teacher forward costing ~25% of a step; bench_pretrain --secs 60 with the 24 s / 36 s split gave 548 steps = 9.09 steps/s including setup and two model builds), falsified if total < 3,200 (then the teacher forward or the second build cost far more than measured); student epochs 1.6-2.1; teacher val loss at 120 s 0.083-0.092; student final val loss 0.082-0.092 (153: 0.0883) and final train CE 0.060-0.075 (153: 0.055); final kd_loss 0.010-0.030 nats; heldout_greedy 0.950-0.975 (153: 0.9675); RL round-1 targets solved 730-820 (153: 766), round-4 1,110-1,200 (153: 1,157); sampling >= 220 samples/s (bench 235; 153: 225-256); total 1,650-1,900 s (153: 1,741). If the student's train CE ends <= 0.055 the anti-memorization mechanism did not operate; if kd_loss ends > 0.05 the student failed to match the teacher and the result says nothing about distillation.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 153-claude; the handoff model is the student built by the same build() (ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8), PeriLNBlock d_ff 1280, fork _init + orthogonal_ on 2D block/MTP params)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 153-claude: no architecture change. Two models of this architecture exist during pretraining (teacher, then student); the teacher and both MTP modules are dropped at handoff.
arch.n_params_detail: handoff model 9,557,760 (bench_pretrain on an A40 with this pretrain.py reported n_params 9,557,760; same breakdown as 153). During phase 2 the frozen teacher (9,557,760, requires_grad False) and the student's MTP module (1,875,584) are also resident; peak memory 7.42 GB in bench.
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged (caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check cached vs full forward max abs logit diff 1.4e-6 at width 384

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: unchanged per phase: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express on hidden matrices + head.weight, AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms, MTP matrices under Muon. Each phase builds fresh optimizer state (Muon momentum buffers, AdamW moments) for its own model; nothing is carried from teacher to student except the teacher's frozen weights used for the KD target.
optimizer.schedule: per phase: 200-step linear warmup then cosine over the phase's wall-clock window, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = (elapsed - t_start) / (t_end - t_start); teacher window [0, 120 s] of the budget (setup ~15 s included, as the incumbent's schedule includes it), student window [120 s, 300 s]; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor. The incumbent ran one cosine over the whole 300 s.

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: student GPT weights only; the teacher, both MTP modules and all pretraining optimizer state are discarded; frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760
optimizer.active_window: teacher: 0-120 s of the budget; student: 120-300 s

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: unchanged token-budget batches (TOK_BUDGET 18,432); token_batches() draws from the same GPU generator and random.Random(seed) stream across both phases, so the student's epochs continue the permutation stream where the teacher's stopped
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: unchanged rule for both models: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)); the student's init draws the next numbers of the harness-seeded torch RNG after the teacher's build, so it is deterministic per seed but a different draw

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token CE on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss, train_loss and last_loss use this term only)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.kd: phase 2 only: KL(p_teacher || p_student) = sum_v p_t(v) * (log p_t(v) - log p_s(v)) at temperature 1 over the same proof-token positions as main (weights m[:, 1:]), mean over those positions; teacher logits from one no-grad forward of the frozen phase-1 model on the same (shift-augmented) batch, softmax in fp32
loss.total: teacher: main + 0.3 * mtp (identical to 153). Student: main + 0.3 * mtp + KD_WEIGHT * kd, KD_WEIGHT = 1.0, constant
loss.curve: curve points every 15 s carry phase ('teacher' | 'student'), train_loss (main CE), val_loss of the model currently training, mtp_loss and kd_loss (None in phase 1); the val curve restarts from ~4.8 at the 120 s phase switch

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence; budget 60 s so the split fell at 24 s): 548 steps in 60.3 s = 9.09 steps/s over both phases including ~15 s setup and two model builds, peak 7.42 GB, n_params 9,557,760, sampling 235 samples/s (153's bench: 695 steps / 11.53 steps/s, 179 samples/s), student val loss 0.336 after its 36 s
